query: The Front Row You cut through the first-years' lecture on your way somewhere else. In the front row, alone, sits a first-year with red ink on her fingers. The lecturer asks her a question. She opens her mouth, and nothing comes out, and the hall waits until she looks at the floor. {flag(red_ink_glimpse): The robes are the ones from the stair, two sizes too big.|Her notes, you can see from the aisle, are perfect.} Sit by her afterwards, and write You sit down beside her after the hall empties and slide your last essay across, without a word. She writes on it for twenty minutes without looking up. At the bottom: "Seminar on Thursday. I have to speak. I can't." Leave her the secret You walk on, and leave your next essay on the stair as usual. It comes back with the usual red, and one line more at the bottom: "Seminar on Thursday. I have to speak. Please don't come."

A Question in the Margin

results.excerpt:
Still Waiting
There's a note in red ink tucked into the crack in the lecture tower stair, in the small round hand you know. It says only: "Still waiting for the next draft. Paragraph four is still the best thing you've written. Don't make it the last."
